title: IndoToxic2024: A Demographically-Enriched Dataset of Hate Speech and Toxicity Types for Indonesian Language

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating within-group and between-group inter-coder reliability among different religious annotators, cross-training models on specific religious groups (e.g., Islam vs. Non-Islam) to test on others, and analyzing zero-shot LLM performance when prompted with the annotator's religion.

Comparing the proportion of texts labeled as toxic by male versus female annotators, analyzing inter-coder reliability across gender lines, and measuring F1 score variations when hate speech models are prompted with annotator gender.

Analyzing model performance and annotator disagreement on texts targeting specific ethnic and national groups (e.g., Chinese, Rohingya refugees) and measuring the impact of including the annotator's ethnicity in the model's prompt.

Using chi-square testing to evaluate the distribution of hate speech assignments across annotator domiciles and analyzing how prompting an LLM with the annotator's specific location (e.g., Medan, Makassar) affects detection performance for localized topics.

Calculating inter-coder reliability among disabled versus non-disabled annotators and measuring shifts in hate speech detection performance when the model is provided with annotator disability status and text topic information.
Examining annotator subjectivity and variations in model performance on texts specifically targeting LGBTQ+ communities by using the annotator's LGBTQ+ identity as a demographic prompt constraint.
Assessing how text classification performance changes across different target topics when the model's demographic prompt includes the annotator's generation or age group.
Evaluating changes in hate speech classification performance when demographic prompts explicitly include the annotator's political leaning (presidential vote preference).

Analyzing instances of annotator disagreement that split along educational backgrounds rather than other demographics, and tracking model F1 score variations when prompted with the annotator's job status and education level.
